correctness.rationale: An order ideal is a nested sequence of layers, each one of the six square lower ideals; conversely any such sequence defines an ideal. Using this independent enumeration and layer-major bit indexing, I reproduced the entire integer Walsh census for all six widths. Width six has 336 ideals, no zeros in degrees 0–2 and 32 triples. The orbit representatives and all four images of each agree exactly with direct parity sums, with no overlaps. Coordinate exchange preserves ideals; complement after reversal is an ideal bijection and multiplies the reversed character sum by (−1)^|S|. Complete zero counts for widths 1–6 are 6,61,680,0,107510,1414094, with least vanishing degrees 1,2,1,none,1,3. Fourier diagonalization gives rank 15363122 at width six and the singular values on the recoverable range have endpoints 2 and 336, hence condition number 168. The exact transform of the complementary frequency mask verifies that the absolute sum of the unnormalized recoverable-support kernel is 9182696964; division by 2^24 reduces to 2295674241/4194304. Convolution by the normalized kernel has ℓ¹ norm equal to its total absolute mass (test a point mass), and the same ℓ∞ norm (choose a sign vector aligned to one row). For any projection onto the range, its translation conjugates all fix that same space and all have image in it; their average remains a projection and its norm is no higher. Translation commutation diagonalizes it in the Walsh basis: identity on surviving characters, zero on lost ones. This proves the unrestricted real and complex minima. ‘32 triple orbits’ in the prior-work prose is a slip; the precise Finding, table and certificate consistently give 32 triples in eight orbits. The argument and all operators are finite-dimensional.
correctness.replay: The frozen check.cpp was inspected, not run. From /workspace/reproductions run python3 5_layers.py n with NumPy >=2, one width at a time for n=1,…,6 (5_width1.log through 5_width6.log; 5_slice.log was the initial small run). The code enumerates nested layer ideals, directly checks every weight ≤3 multiplier against the full transform, checks Parseval and uses the complementary rather than surviving frequency mask to compute the final kernel norm. Signed-32-bit butterfly magnitudes are bounded by the indicator support size, at most 2^24 for either transform, and sums of magnitudes and squares use 64-bit integers. The proof of optimality is independent of computation.

value.rationale: The canonical 2×2×n family gives a motivated finite least-degree cutoff, separating protection of first- and second-order parity information from cubic information loss. The orbit census specifies the lost low-order observables, while the rank, restricted condition number and exact optimal endpoint amplification supply complementary recovery benchmarks. These values concern this natural family and are not a restatement of the unsigned count; no larger-width theory is claimed.
